coherence.statement: Zones have one rule: feed separation is SM's routing (Z01) or a post-match filter (Z04), never both, and D09 keeps what that rule reads (`extract_zone` for routing).
Bare East/West are stripped for scoring (N02) only when a zone rule enforces feeds afterwards; N10 is N02's bare-region switch.
`(P)` reads as no zone (Z07 `sm-strict`) only under SM's routing (Z01 `sm-zone`) with no post-match filter reading `(p)` (Z04 `none`).

Trailing tags strip before the zone read (Z08 `strip-tags`) only under SM's unguarded routing (Z01 `sm-zone`, Z02 `none`: `sm_zone_noguard` is the one zone read that strips) with no post-match filter reading original names (Z04 `none`).
The prefix order fits the prefix table (N12 `first` with the core's N04).
Designator repair (N08) exactly when the digit guard (T07) reads designator tokens.
One callsign ladder: C01-C04 are one CALLSIGN configuration; the anchor (D04) reads high-confidence callsigns only, so the loose OTA-number rescue (C04, low confidence) has nothing to feed.

Callsign-first (C07 `callsign-first`) needs the merged allowlist (C02 `merged`) and extends the high-confidence anchor (D04 `jan-lu-anchor`): the query's callsign only counts when it is high-confidence and the merged station table knows it.

The ranker is LU's match_all_streams shape (T09), which carries the always-majority floor (T02), the guarded exact tier (T04), scaled thresholds (T05), the header skip (Z05) and LU's country rule (G01-G03, strict only once a country is configured).
Aliases resolve through one index: `identity` (A01) is CM's reverse index (A02) over the merged table (A03).

C07.reason: Orchestrator decision (follow-up engine fix, plan step-15 review): when the query's identity has a high-confidence callsign (the engine's existing confidence) that exists in the merged station table, a candidate with the same callsign outranks any non-callsign match, and a candidate with a DIFFERENT known callsign is excluded (the C06/D04 anchor's high/high hard-reject, extended to any known candidate callsign); a candidate with no callsign (the bare national `ABC`) only wins when no same-callsign candidate survives the cut in the pool (fallback keeps today's behaviour for pools that lack the station). Identity families stay consistent: callsign identities already ignore country (bug-161), unchanged. No plugin variant ranks callsign-first (LU's anchor only decides high/high pairs; nothing reorders a same-callsign 95 above a stripped-key Exact 100), so there is no variant to ablate. Implemented in Rust's `score_core` (step 2a: different known callsign excluded) + `ranked_survivors` (same callsign sorts before any higher-scoring non-callsign candidate) and mirrored in the decided Python configuration (`ablate.Engine.score` + `engine_parity.python_family` via `callsign_first_base` / `candidate_known_base` over the merged table). Corpus effect under the decided configuration: engine cost 844 at cut 80 (unchanged: FP 34, FN 776) and 835 at cut 95 (unchanged: FP 8, FN 819) — the old high/high anchor already rejected the corpus pairs this extends, and no construction pair sets a known low-confidence rival callsign against a station query; the four network-led examples (`ABC (WABC)`, `US: ABC (WABC) HD`, `NBC (KSDK)`, `CBS (WFOR) [HD]`) now rank the station family with the station in the pool and the national family without it. `13 WREX` unchanged; names without a callsign never trigger the rule. Step-15 C07 review audit: over every name in the merged channel DBs, lineups, alias tables and corpus (60,745), no pair a high-confidence station query matched before C07 (cut 95 through the Rust engine on every word-sharing candidate; cut 80 through this mirror on 517,447 candidate pairs sharing half their words) carries a different known callsign, so the exclusion removes nothing today; the only non-station words it reads as known callsigns are `Tyne & Wear TV` (WEAR) and `Hong Kong Fight Club` (KONG), neither near a station query. The national fallback keeps Janitor's answer: Janitor assigns the bare national entry to `ABC (WABC)` whether or not the station is listed (the oracle reports' `C07-callsign-first` probes); a network feed's guide is right for the network day and wrong for local news, which beats no guide, and no evidence asks for an AI/rescue gate instead.

N15.reason: Orchestrator decision (phase 3 step 14, step-14 review): before keying and before the zone/country reads, the engine treats `|` as a segment separator and drops segments that are pure junk per the shared vocabulary (`tags::is_pipe_junk_segment`, the ONE definition from step 14: single NC quality/junk tokens, `\d{3,4}p`, `FHD\d+`, `H.265`/`H.264` spellings, one bracket layer peeled, only `sources` containing `NC`), then joins the survivors with a space. A country code (the core's delimited-prefix codes) keeps a delimiter the core's tables already strip, so no bare country word is stranded: a segment ending in a code joins with `: ` (`UK | Sky Sports` -> `UK: Sky Sports`; `RK: US | CNN` -> `RK: US: CNN`, keyed `CNN` like `US | CNN`) and a final code-only segment keeps its bar (`BBC One | UK`, the core's trailing strip). A lone code is not a marker, so `USA | HD |` (USA Network) collapses to `USA` and stays country-less, like the cleaned name. Joining the code with a bare space instead stranded `US` (`RK: US CNN`, `BBC One UK`) and flipped N14 to Janitor's bare `USA?\s` anywhere strip, which keys `X USA FHD` and `HD X USA` differently. No plugin variant strips pipe segments before matching, so there is no variant to ablate. Effect under the decided configuration: `Cinemax East | HD |` keys as `cinemax` with zone East (was `cinemax | |`, Default); `UK | Sky Sports | HD` -> country UK, key `sky sports`; `HD | UK | Sky One` -> country UK; names with a meaningful pipe segment keep both parts (`Sky Sports | Premier League` -> `Sky Sports Premier League`). Byte-identical Rust/Python on every corpus name bare and pipe-decorated (`engine_parity.py` kind `pipe`).
